name: Semal Heights
description:
Four residential towers of twenty floors on the Airport Road side of Mohali, planned around a landscaped central court. Homes are three- and four-bedroom apartments, with a small number of penthouses on the upper floors, and every apartment has a deep balcony facing either the court or the open sectors to the south.

Airport Road puts the international airport, IT City and the Aerocity business district a short drive away, with the southern sectors of Chandigarh reached along the same road.

name: Kachnar Township
description:
A gated township on the Peer Muchalla side of Zirakpur, laid out as low-rise apartment blocks, independent floors and a pocket of residential plots behind a single controlled entrance. The blocks are set around three neighbourhood parks rather than one showpiece lawn, so no home is far from open space, and the internal roads are lined with kachnar and amaltas trees.

Peer Muchalla sits between Panchkula and Zirakpur, with the southern sectors of Panchkula and the Zirakpur highway junction both close by, and schools, markets and hospitals within the locality.

name: Siswan Ridge Villas
description:
A low-density community of independent villas in Mullanpur, New Chandigarh, where the plain meets the first ridges of the Shivaliks. Each villa stands on its own plot with a private front and rear garden, and building heights are kept low so the hills stay in view from the internal streets.

Mullanpur is quieter and greener than the older sectors of the Tricity, with the Siswan forest to the north and the northern sectors of Chandigarh a short drive to the east.

name: Sarson Fields
description:
A plotted residential development off the Kharar–Landran road, with plots in several sizes on a grid of wide internal roads. The layout sets aside a central park and a neighbourhood market, so a family building here has open space and daily shopping inside the gate.

The Landran road links Kharar with the education belt at Landran and the newer sectors of Mohali, and the Chandigarh–Kharar highway is a few minutes away.

name: Copperleaf Square
description:
A row of shop-cum-office (SCO) buildings on the PR-7 airport road in Zirakpur. Each SCO is a self-contained building of ground plus three floors with its own stair and lift, so a floor can be let on its own or the whole building used by one business, and every unit fronts a service lane with parking in front.

PR-7 carries the airport traffic between Zirakpur and Mohali and has become one of the busier retail corridors of the Tricity.
